basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Dixit itaque Dominus: Clamor Sodomorum et Gomorrhae multiplicatus est, et peccatum eorum'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Dixit itaque Dominus: Clamor Sodomorum et Gomorrhae multiplicatus est, et peccatum eorum aggravatum est nimis. Clamorem Sodomorum scelerum famam vel potius infamiam dicit, a quo nos prohibens Apostolus dicit: Omnis amaritudo, et ira, et indignatio, et clamor, et blasphemia, tollatur a vobis cum omni malitia (Ephes. IV, 31); cui nimirum clamori contrarius est clamor electorum, de quo confidenter suo Creatori supplicantes, aiunt dicentes singuli: Domine, exaudi orationem meam, et clamor meus ad te perveniat (Psal. CI, 2). Magnus quippe illorum clamor est meritum sublime et intentio fidei coelestia sola quaerens, ubi Christus est in dextera Dei sedens; qui quoniam non terrenas opes, non gloriam inanem caducamque, non moritura carnis gaudia, sed superna tantum bona, desiderant, altum profecto et quasi clamore personum est omne quod agunt. Verum multiplicato clamore peccatorum, id est enormi illorum scelere, videamus quid sequitur.
